name: Kevin Holland
summary: A long, talkative welterweight veteran (29-15, 1 NC; 16-12, 1 NC in the UFC) from Phalanx MMA Academy. He beat Randy Brown by decision in April to end a two-fight skid, then withdrew from two bookings against Jacobe Smith (July and October) because of injuries, per Sherdog. This will be his first fight in seven months. He is dangerous everywhere but has been out-wrestled and out-grappled by top opponents.

how_they_fight.Striking: Rangy kickboxer: about 4.5 significant strikes a minute at 51%, absorbing 3.1. Against Brown his calf kicks damaged the lead leg and a left hand dropped Brown in R1, though Brown buckled him with a left hook and cut him (Cageside). Sherdog's Tom Feely wrote in April that at welterweight he has leaned on his size to hunt knockouts, with 'less flashes of his prior technical craft'. Fourteen KO/TKO wins.
how_they_fight.Grappling: A real submission threat: nine submission wins, including Vicente Luque (R2, 2025), Michal Oleksiejczuk (R1, 2024) and Michael Chiesa (R1, 2023). He locked an anaconda choke on Brown in R2 and threatened guillotines (Cageside). Rarely shoots himself (about 0.8 takedowns per 15).
how_they_fight.Defense: Hard to knock out: only two KO/TKO losses, both against top opposition (Stephen Thompson after R4 in 2022; Roman Dolidze at the end of R1 in 2024). The hole is being held down. Derek Brunson and Marvin Vettori controlled him for about 17 and 20 minutes in five-round fights in 2021, Khamzat Chimaev and Reinier de Ridder submitted him in R1, and Gunnar Nelson held him for over nine minutes in a fight Holland still won. Feely notes takedown defense has been a recurring problem.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Finishes come throughout the fight: of 23 stoppage wins, 13 came in R1, five in R2 and five in R3. He has gone the distance in nine of his 15 losses (seven three-rounders, two five-rounders); his other losses were submissions (three in R1, one in R2) and the two TKOs (R1, R4). His last three fights all went to decisions (losses to Daniel Rodriguez and Mike Malott, the win over Brown). Feely noted Malott beat him while he was still affected by a low blow.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Loose and chatty in the cage. Keeps a busy schedule; he said in July he usually fights two or three times a year and wants to reach about 38 UFC fights before retiring (LowKick). His activity has slipped in 2026 because of the two withdrawals.

patterns: Kicks the legs and body from long range
Dangerous submission game in scrambles (anaconda, guillotine)
Rarely knocked out; two KO/TKO losses in 45 fights
Loses to wrestlers who hold him down for long stretches
concerns: Seven months out and two injury withdrawals since April
Gets hit while hunting his own shots: Brown buckled and cut him in R1
Medić's early power: he has to get through R1 cleanly
Lost three of his last five before the Brown win
keys_to_beat: Wrestle him and hold top position; long control has beaten him repeatedly
Be careful in scrambles; don't give him the neck
Pressure him and make him exchange inside, rather than letting him kick from range

news.text: Withdrew from bouts against Jacobe Smith at UFC Oklahoma City in July and UFC 332 in October; Sherdog says both were because of injuries.
After beating Randy Brown, Jacobe Smith called Holland out again and said he is 'scared' of him. No response from Holland was reported.
Beat Randy Brown by unanimous decision (30-27 x3) at UFC 327, with a knockdown and an anaconda choke attempt.
Booked against Uroš Medić on the UFC 334 main card.
